s1.syndrome_frame: A subareolar breast mass with a history of gynecomastia
salient_findings: persistent swelling of the left breast
a new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass
a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography
key_facts: 29-year-old healthy man
persistent swelling of the left breast for four years
history of anabolic-steroid use
anabolic-steroid use was discontinued
new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple
ultrasonography shows a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture
mammography reveals a lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter
no microcalcifications on mammography
initial ultrasonography had shown gynecomastia (BIRADS II)

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of anabolic-steroid use, which is a known cause of gynecomastia, and initial ultrasonography showed gynecomastia (BIRADS II). Although a new mass has developed, the presence of a lobular architecture on ultrasonography and a lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography could still be consistent with gynecomastia, especially given the patient's history.

rejected.label: Breast cancer in men
rejected.why: No microcalcifications on mammography and the mass has a lobular architecture, which is less typical for breast cancer

rejected.label: Pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia
rejected.why: Not directly related to the patient's history of anabolic-steroid use or the described imaging findings

rejected.label: Fibroadenoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a well-circumscribed mass, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents as a rapidly growing mass, which is not indicated in the vignette

rejected.label: Papilloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with nipple discharge, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: Similar reasoning as for breast cancer in men, with no strong evidence to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Intraductal papilloma
rejected.why: Usually presents with nipple discharge and is often smaller than the described mass
